page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-64 is an arm64-based server instance powered by the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration, ensuring no hyperthreading overhead. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Cache specifications include 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 80 MB L3 cache. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data highlights strong memory performance and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieved a top-tier rating in small-block cached read memory bandwidth at 7912.04 GB/sec, alongside a PassMark memory score of 3278.13. Multi-core processing is robust, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 115712.52 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 717.79 GB/sec. Database and web serving operations are highly efficient, with Redis SET operations reaching 134.03 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured at 122.37 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4a-highmem-64 leverages the ARM architecture to deliver high resource density and strong memory bandwidth per resource unit. This makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and multi-threaded data processing. It is well-suited for high-throughput web serving, Redis caching layers, and medium-scale language model inference, though the lack of local storage requires external network-attached storage solutions.
